title: Slow consumer
summary: A client that fetches a few rows and then pauses: each session runs a wide query (about 1 KB per row) and the runner reads its result set slowly on purpose, so the server fills the network buffers and waits for the client (ASYNC_NETWORK_IO). At the deadline or on a stop request the runner cancels the query, and while the run lasts it runs the query again. The procedure only reads.

intensity.description: How slowly the client reads: 25 rows, then a pause of about 100 ms at 1 up to 1 second at 10.

notes.T1: The runner on the same VM is the client; the wait is the same.
notes.T2: The runner in the guest is the client; the wait is the same.
notes.T3: The client is T1's runner, across the network: the usual shape of a slow application against Azure SQL Database.

rowsPerQuery.description: Rows each query returns at most (about 1 KB each).

expectedHubSignals.signal: SqlServerWaitStats: Network IO wait category (ASYNC_NETWORK_IO), one long wait per session
SqlServerPerformanceCountersCommon: SQL Attention rate above 0 when the runner cancels a query
SqlServerActiveSessions: the ContosoCare.Demo/slow-consumer sessions running for minutes

expectedSymptoms: ASYNC_NETWORK_IO dominating the waits while the server itself is mostly idle
Long-running requests that do little work: the client, not the server, sets the pace
queryLevelEvidence: sys.dm_exec_requests: wait_type ASYNC_NETWORK_IO on the ContosoCare.Demo/slow-consumer sessions (needs VIEW SERVER STATE or VIEW DATABASE STATE)
The runner's run outcome: rows read, queries, and cancellations per session
reset: Read-only: nothing to undo. The runner cancels its queries and closes its sessions; reset kills any that remain.
